title: Mammalian sweet taste receptors
authors: Nelson G, Hoon MA, Chandrashekar J, Zhang Y, Ryba NJ, Zuker CS
population: HEK-293 cells expressing rat T1R2 and T1R3 with promiscuous G proteins; transgenic mice
funder: This work was supported in part by a grant from the National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders to C.Z. C.Z. is an investigator of the Howard Hughes Medical Institute.
result: T1Rs are G protein-coupled receptors of taste receptor cells, and the Sac locus encodes T1R3. Cells co-expressing rat T1R2 and T1R3 raised intracellular calcium in response to sucrose, fructose, saccharin, acesulfame K, dulcin and two guanidinoacetic acid sweeteners, but not to glucose, galactose, maltose or aspartame; neither subunit alone responded, so the two function as a heteromeric receptor. Rodents do not taste aspartame, and human and rodent T1Rs are only about 70% identical.
